questions.q:
Violence escalated in Jonglei State in March 2026. Consider the following countries:
1. Sudan
2. Ethiopia
3. Uganda
4. Kenya
5. Chad
How many of the above share a land border with the country in which Jonglei lies?
questions.e: Jonglei is in South Sudan, whose capital is Juba, and the first four are its neighbours, along with DR Congo and the Central African Republic. Chad does not touch it; Chad borders Sudan to the west and the Central African Republic to the south. South Sudan is landlocked and the world's youngest country, having gained independence in 2011. The White Nile and the vast Sudd wetland lie in this region, and competition over land and cattle is a recurring factor in conflict.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 94; borders are static

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs:
Place in the news : State/UT
1. Gurez Valley : Ladakh
2. Kavaratti : Lakshadweep
3. Dharali : Himachal Pradesh
4. Mahad : Maharashtra
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Pairs 2 and 4 are correct. Kavaratti in Lakshadweep is the site of India's first integrated ocean thermal energy plant, and Mahad, in Raigad district of Maharashtra, is where the Chawdar Tank Satyagraha began in 1927. Pair 1 is wrong: Gurez Valley, where mobile units carried out intensive TB screening, lies in Jammu and Kashmir. Pair 3 is wrong: Dharali, hit by the 2025 flash flood that ISRO traced to an ice-patch collapse on the Srikanta Glacier, is in Uttarakhand.
questions.s: Shankar IAS pp. 28-30; Vision IAS pp. 53-54, 58, 83-84

questions.q:
With reference to places in the news during the West Asia war, consider the following statements:
1. Fujairah lies on the Gulf of Oman, so oil exported from it avoids the Strait of Hormuz.
2. Kharg Island, the terminal for most of Iran's crude exports, lies in the Caspian Sea.
3. Tyre, a coastal city of southern Lebanon caught in the conflict zone, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Fujairah sits just outside the strait on the Gulf of Oman, which lets the UAE ship oil without passing through Hormuz. Tyre, an ancient Phoenician port, is a World Heritage city that was exposed to strikes in southern Lebanon. Statement 2 is wrong: Kharg Island, which handles about 90 per cent of Iran's crude exports, lies in the Persian Gulf. The Caspian Sea lies to Iran's north and served as an Iran-Russia supply route that Israel struck.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 14-15, 18; Tyre heritage status is static

questions.q:
Yaounde hosted the 14th WTO Ministerial Conference. Which of the following statements is/are correct about the host country?
1. Cameroon has a coastline on the Gulf of Guinea.
2. Yaounde is Cameroon's main Atlantic seaport.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. Cameroon, in west-central Africa, has a coast on the Gulf of Guinea. Statement 2 is wrong: Yaounde, the capital, lies inland on a plateau, and Douala is the chief port and commercial hub. Capitals are often confused with main ports in this way. Cameroon borders Nigeria, Chad, the Central African Republic, Gabon, Equatorial Guinea and the Republic of Congo. The ministerial conference itself dealt with matters like the e-commerce moratorium and the Appellate Body.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 94; Cameroon geography is static

questions.q: Scientists decoded the evolution of the Ladakh Magmatic Arc. A magmatic arc is best described as
o: a ring of impact craters created by ancient meteorite strikes
a belt of igneous rocks formed above a subduction zone
a curved line of glacial moraines left at the foot of a mountain range
a chain of sedimentary basins formed by river deposition along a transform fault
questions.e: When an oceanic plate descends beneath another plate, melting produces magma that rises to form a belt of igneous rock. In the north-west Himalaya, this is tied to the closure of the Tethys Ocean as the Indian Plate moved north under Eurasia, before the continental collision. River basins, glacial moraines and impact craters arise from wholly different processes and do not involve subduction melting. Studying the arc therefore helps reconstruct the Himalayan collision story, which is a staple of geomorphology.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 93; Tethys context is static

questions.q:
Statement-I: The Atacama Desert is among the driest non-polar regions on Earth.
Statement-II: The Andes block moisture-bearing winds from the east.
Statement-III: The cold Humboldt Current off the coast limits the moisture available for rain.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct and both of them explain Statement-I
Both Statement-II and Statement-III are correct, but only one of them explains Statement-I
Only one of Statement-II and Statement-III is correct and that explains Statement-I
Neither Statement-II nor Statement-III is correct
questions.e: All are correct, and both later statements explain the first. The Andes create a rain shadow, while the cold offshore current stabilises the air and suppresses rainfall from the Pacific side. This extreme dryness makes Salar de Pajonales in Chile a useful Mars analogue: scientists are studying its gypsum deposits to learn how minerals and any possible life signals might survive in harsh conditions. Chile also forms part of the lithium-rich zone, which adds economic importance to this salt-flat landscape.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 94; causes of aridity are static

questions.q: Salar de Pajonales in Chile's Atacama Desert was in the news in March 2026 because
o: it was chosen as the site of the world's largest new lithium brine extraction project
a glacial lake outburst flood from it devastated settlements in northern Chile
it hosts the Atacama Large Millimeter Array, which detected the most distant megamaser
scientists are studying its gypsum deposits, since its harsh conditions closely resemble those on Mars
questions.e: Researchers are studying gypsum deposits at Salar de Pajonales because the extreme dryness, high radiation and salt chemistry of this Atacama salt flat make it a close analogue of Mars, useful for judging how minerals might preserve signs of life. It is not a new lithium project, although Chile lies in the lithium-rich zone. The ALMA observatory stands on the Chajnantor plateau, and the record megamaser was found by South Africa's MeerKAT. A glacial outburst does not fit a hyper-arid basin.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 81, 94; ALMA location is static

questions.q:
The Litani River was in the news due to the Israel-Lebanon conflict. Which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. It lies wholly within Lebanon and drains into the Mediterranean Sea.
2. It rises in Syria and forms the border between Syria and Israel.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. The Litani rises in the Bekaa Valley and flows south, then turns west to reach the Mediterranean north of Tyre, without leaving Lebanon, so statement 2 is wrong and it is not a boundary river. Discussions in Israel about moving its northern border up to the Litani drew attention because such a change would involve territory well inside Lebanon. The Jordan River and the Golan area, by contrast, relate to the Syria-Israel frontier, which is the likely source of confusion.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 94; Bekaa source is static

questions.q:
With reference to Santiniketan, which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. It was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2023.
2. The Basant Utsav celebrated there is a tradition started by Rabindranath Tagore at Visva-Bharati.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Both are correct. Santiniketan in West Bengal, the home of Tagore's Visva-Bharati, got its World Heritage listing as a cultural site in 2023. The spring festival, begun by Tagore, celebrates the season with music and dance and was in the news again this year. The institution itself reflected his idea of learning close to nature, with open-air classes and a blend of Indian and global ideas. Visva-Bharati later became a central university, a fact that often appears in questions.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 93; central university status is static

questions.q:
Statement-I: Ships passing through the Panama Canal are raised and lowered by locks.
Statement-II: The canal's central section runs through an artificial lake situated well above sea level.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct, but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct, but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect, but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both are correct, and the second explains the first. The canal, opened in 1914 and about 82 km long, uses locks to lift vessels to Gatun Lake and then lower them on the other side, linking the Atlantic through the Caribbean with the Pacific. This makes it reliant on rainfall for fresh water, unlike the sea-level Suez Canal. It worked at full capacity in March 2026, as the Iran war increased LNG tanker traffic, and droughts in recent years have shown that this route has its limits.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 94; Gatun Lake and Suez contrast are static

questions.q:
Which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. Chabahar Port lies on the Gulf of Oman and thus outside the Strait of Hormuz.
2. The Salma Dam, known as the Afghan-India Friendship Dam, is on the Kabul River in eastern Afghanistan.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Only statement 1 is correct. Chabahar, in Iran's Sistan-Baluchestan province, faces the Gulf of Oman, so its traffic does not pass through Hormuz, which adds to its appeal for India's access to Afghanistan and Central Asia. Statement 2 is wrong on location: Salma Dam is on the Hari Rud in Herat province in western Afghanistan, not on the Kabul River. Both projects figure in India's connectivity diplomacy, and the conflicts around both countries raise fresh risks to them.
questions.s: Vision IAS pp. 20-21; river and province are static

questions.q:
India sent rice to Malawi as drought relief in March 2026. Consider the following countries:
1. Tanzania
2. Zambia
3. Mozambique
4. Zimbabwe
5. Angola
How many of the above share a land border with Malawi?
questions.e: Tanzania, Zambia and Mozambique border Malawi. Zimbabwe lies close to it, but a strip of Mozambique's Tete province separates the two. Angola is farther to the west, beyond Zambia. Malawi is a landlocked state in south-east Africa whose capital is Lilongwe, and Lake Malawi marks much of its eastern side. Landlocked status raises the cost of imports during a drought, which is part of the reason humanitarian shipments by partners such as India matter.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 94; borders are static

questions.q:
Shigellosis cases were reported in Kerala. Consider the following statements:
1. It is a viral infection transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes.
2. It is a diarrhoeal disease spread through contaminated food and water.
3. Small children are especially vulnerable to it.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Shigellosis is caused by Shigella bacteria and spreads through the faecal-oral route, so statement 1 is wrong on both organism and vector; Aedes spreads viral diseases such as dengue. Young children face higher risk because a small dose may cause illness and dehydration can follow. Clean water, sanitation and handwashing are the main defences, and growing antibiotic resistance makes prevention more important, which is why outbreaks are closely tracked by health authorities.
questions.s: Vision IAS p. 93; vulnerability of children is static
